scientificCalculator.title: Scientific Calculator
scientificCalculator.subtitle: From basic arithmetic to trig, logs, powers and factorials. Type on your keyboard if you like — the result previews as you write.

errors.paren: Parentheses don't match — there are too many closing ones.
errors.domain: Value is outside the domain (e.g. square root of a negative, log of 0 or less, sin⁻¹ of a value above 1).
errors.undefined: Undefined — the angle has no value, like tan 90°.
errors.overflow: The number is too large to calculate.

guide.title: How to Use the Scientific Calculator

howTo.title: Getting started
items: Build an expression with the number and operator keys and the result previews below it. Press = to show the result in large type and save it to the history.
After a result, pressing an operator such as + − × ÷ continues from the previous answer (Ans). Pressing a number starts a new expression.
Function keys such as sin, log and √ insert the opening parenthesis for you. If you forget to close it, = closes it automatically.
On a phone, tap 'Show scientific keys' to reveal trig, log and factorial keys.
Keyboard works too: Enter calculates, Backspace deletes one character, Esc clears everything.
Use the share buttons under the result to copy a link — whoever opens it sees the same expression and result.

order.title: Order of operations
items: Parentheses → functions (sin, log, √ …) → factorial and percent (!, %) → powers (^) → sign (−) → implied multiplication (2π) → nPr and nCr → multiplication and division → addition and subtraction.
Powers are evaluated right to left: 2^3^2 = 2^9 = 512.
−2^2 is −(2^2) = −4. To square a negative number, wrap it: (−2)^2.
Implied multiplication (2π, 3(4+5), 2sin(30)) binds tighter than ÷, so 1÷2π means 1÷(2π).

angle.title: Degrees (DEG) and radians (RAD)
items: This switch sets the angle unit for trig functions. The default is degrees, and your choice is remembered in this browser.
Degrees split a full turn into 360°, radians into 2π. 180° = π radians.
School geometry and physics angles (30°, 45°, 60°) use DEG; calculus and programming formulas usually use RAD.
In DEG, sin 180° and cos 90° are exactly 0 and tan 45° is exactly 1. tan 90° has no value and is reported as 'Undefined'.
Inverse trig results (sin⁻¹, cos⁻¹, tan⁻¹) also use the selected unit: in DEG, sin⁻¹(0.5) = 30.

rows.desc: Trig functions, using the DEG/RAD setting
Inverse trig: angle from a value

items.a: The angle unit is probably set to radians (RAD). Tap DEG at the top of the display to calculate in degrees and sin(30) becomes 0.5. In radians, sin(30) is the sine of 30 radians, which is −0.988.

By the usual math convention, powers are evaluated before the sign: −2^2 = −(2×2) = −4. To square −2, wrap it in parentheses — (−2)^2 = 4. Excel applies the sign first and returns 4, so the two can differ.

Computers store decimals in binary, which leaves tiny errors. This calculator rounds results to 12 significant digits, so you see a clean 0.3. Numbers of 1e15 or more, or below 0.000001, are shown in exponent form such as 1.5E+20.

tan is sin ÷ cos, and cos 90° is 0, so the division has no value. The same goes for 270°, −90° and any angle 180° apart from 90°. Many calculators show a huge number or a generic error here; this one tells you it's undefined.

% divides the number before it by 100: 50% is 0.5 and 200×10% is 20. Unlike some pocket calculators it does not turn 200+10% into 220 — that gives 200.1 — so write 200×(1+10%) for markups or use the percent calculator.

items.q: How large a factorial can it calculate?
items.a: Integers from 0 to 170. 171! is about 1.2×10^309, beyond the largest number a computer can hold (about 1.8×10^308). Factorials of decimals or negative numbers are reported as outside the domain.

items.q: Can I write 2π or 3(4+5) without a multiplication sign?
items.a: Yes. A number followed by a parenthesis, constant or function is multiplied: 2π = 6.283…, 3(4+5) = 27, 2sin(30) = 1. This implied multiplication binds tighter than ÷, so 1÷2π means 1÷(2π).

Only the last 20 calculations are saved, in this browser's localStorage, and nothing is sent to a server. It isn't shared across devices, and you can remove it with 'Clear history' or by clearing your browser data.
